title: Modernity's descent into Mediocrity: Scientism, Plastic Idols and Atheist Doom
summary: Educated Barbarian episode on Nietzsche's diagnosis of modernity after the death of God. NH argues religion is a permanent human trait, that science, labor and consumerism became new 'plastic' gods, and that modern morality is Christian morality emptied of faith. The modern 'undermensch' pursues hedonism and escape from pain instead of meaning; the way out is to diagnose this and regain faith and true hope.
claims: Religion is a human trait, not a primitive one: the need to explain where we come from and where we go means it will never disappear even as science advances
When God died nothing valuable replaced him; idolatry remained but people now worship TV, celebrities, media and products without the spiritual benefits ancient worship gave
Modern Western countries kept Christian morality but dropped the faith, keeping the skeleton of religion without the flesh, which is why morals feel fake and are eroding
Nietzsche saw Schopenhauer's pessimism as a bastardized half-Christian half-German sensibility; modern pessimists secretly hope to be proven wrong
Nietzsche is not against morals, only against empty tenets with no meaning; the answer lies beyond the historical construction of good and evil
The Ubermensch is world-approving and exuberant, accepts nature as it is and wants it to remain so; modernity is anti-nature (concrete towers, cutting trees)
Science became the new god: most people follow it not because they understand it but because it is the strongest, most omnipotent god available
Any system seeking absolute answers becomes corrupt; science denies what it cannot explain (e.g. the soul) just as ancient faith was corrupted
Industriousness is anti-spiritual: constant productivity kills the idleness required for self-discovery and connection with a higher being
NH's own thesis (not Nietzsche's): the industrial revolution engineered us to love work and resent aristocratic leisure, preparing the ground for the new god
Many people are depressed because they know neither where they come from nor where they are going; we are worker bees that lost the queen
Social media, drugs, capitalism and nationalism are the modern opium; critics can spot others' opium but not the one they smoke
Most atheists are passive (they believe in nothing); active atheists preach like a church; atheism is a continuation of Christianity
Modern humanist tolerance comes directly from Christianity; atheists who think they evolved past religious men ignore their own lineage
Christianity presented man as grey, neither wholly good nor evil, making religion one of the first forms of psychology
Distinguish selfish individualism (surface-level, barely knowing oneself) from introspective individualism, which builds strong humans and communities; the West is selfishly individualistic
The modern form of worship is hedonism: eat, get fat, take drugs, watch TV; such people seem happy on the surface but are miserable deep down
More than pleasure, modern people want escape from pain; rejecting biology and denaturing oneself is the slaves' revenge against nature
The way out is to diagnose modernity as a corpse and regain faith and true hope, whether in God or something else
